models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light-air, flat-sea pattern over the Aeolians - benign if it holds, but far too early to bank on the trip dates.
briefing.synopsis: Current consensus across ECMWF IFS and AIFS (both 02 Oct 06Z) and ICON-2i (02 Oct 12Z) shows a slack, low-gradient pattern over the islands: winds mostly 2-6 kt with no sustained direction, swinging from E/SE overnight through N/NE by midday, and seas running 0.1-0.5 ft. Gusts of 9-14 kt appear in the IFS field, but that is an interval maximum in very light air rather than a real squall signal. There is no organised pressure feature in the data to describe, and nothing in the payload indicates a change through the end of the model window on 08 Oct - which is not the same as saying none will develop.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Tonight's berth is Portorosa Marina, an enclosed basin with all-round shelter; the 03 Oct forecast there is SE 4 kt, gusts 9 kt, swell 0.1 ft, so the choice does not matter and nothing in the payload would move the fleet. No alternative is listed and none is needed at these numbers. Treat it as a quiet dockside night.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: For Portorosa → Lipari on 04 Oct the recommended start is 06:00, with SSE around 4 kt, gusts 10 kt, waves 0.1 ft and a downwind angle (TWA 174°) - motoring weather more than sailing weather. Every window from 06:00 to 14:00 scores 'go' on the conservative thresholds, so the morning is about preference, not necessity. Note that at 12:00 local on 04 Oct the models split at Portorosa, 1.6 to 7.8 kt, so do not plan on a specific midday breeze.

passage_notes.note: Go on current data: SSE 4 kt, 0.1 ft, 06:00 start. Wind backs to NNE and goes close-hauled by midday; models disagree 1.6-7.8 kt at noon.
NW-NNW 4-5 kt, gusts to 11 kt, waves 0.1-0.2 ft. Beam to close reach all day, no preferred window.
NW 4-6 kt, gusts to 12 kt, waves building only to 0.5 ft by late afternoon. Early start keeps it shortest.

passage_notes.leg: Stromboli → Panarea, optional return (06 Oct, 11 nm)
passage_notes.note: Very light, 2-4 kt from NE veering E, residual 0.9 ft swell. Expect to motor.
Best breeze of the week: S 8 kt at 06:00 easing to 5 kt and backing NNW, 0.4-0.6 ft.
SSW 5 kt at dawn fading to 2-3 kt by midday, 0.1 ft. Go early if you want to sail at all.

cautions: These figures are five to seven days out. Forecast stability at 72-120 h lead shows a mean wind shift of only 1.0 kt but a mean direction shift of 63 degrees - in air this light the speed is stable and the direction is essentially unforecastable, so plan sail choices on the day.
